findings.title: Async legacy write inherits cancelled request context
findings.body: In Create (and identically in Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) the goroutine does context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) where ctx is the incoming request context that already has the klog value added. When the API request completes the parent context is cancelled, which immediately cancels the child, so the best-effort legacy write can be aborted before it runs. The consequence is the legacy backup silently diverges. The async work must derive from a detached context (e.g. context.WithoutCancel or context.Background) plus timeout.

findings.title: Legacy Create replicates pre-storage input instead of stored result
findings.body: Create writes d.Storage.Create(ctx, obj, ...) to get `created`, but the background goroutine calls d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...) with the original input object. Any defaulting, UID/ResourceVersion, creationTimestamp or mutation performed by unified storage is lost in legacy, leaving the two stores permanently divergent. The legacy call should replicate `created`.

findings.title: Legacy Update reuses same UpdatedObjectInfo concurrently
findings.body: Update calls d.Storage.Update with objInfo and then reuses the identical objInfo interface value in a background goroutine for d.Legacy.Update. UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject() is invoked once per store against different old objects and can be stateful/one-shot; invoking it a second time asynchronously can produce a wrong object, resourceVersion conflict, or data race. The consequence is failed or corrupt legacy writes. Snapshot the updated object from the storage result instead of re-invoking objInfo.

findings.title: Delete records object name as metrics kind label
findings.body: In Delete the success path calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) where the third argument is the metric kind label but `name` (the object name) is passed instead of options.Kind. This mislabels delete latency and creates unbounded high-cardinality label values, one series per object name, which can overload Prometheus.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection recorded as storage duration
findings.body: In DeleteCollection the background legacy call ends with d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). It measures a legacy-store operation but records it with the storage histogram, so legacy latency/errors are invisible and storage metrics are polluted. It should call d.recordLegacyDuration.

findings.title: Storage Create/Update failures recorded as legacy duration
findings.body: In Create on d.Storage.Create error the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...), and Update does the same on d.Storage.Update error at line 129. A storage failure is recorded against the legacy histogram and no storage failure is recorded, inverting observability and alerting. Both error branches should call d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...).

findings.title: Async legacy failures are never logged
findings.body: All four background legacy writes (Create, Delete, Update, DeleteCollection) capture the legacy error only for the err != nil metric flag and then discard it with no log. Unlike the prior synchronous code that logged legacy errors, operators now have no message identifying which object/kind failed to replicate to legacy. Log the legacy error with the request logger before dropping it.

findings.title: Delete discards enriched logger context
findings.body: Delete builds log := d.Log.WithValues(name, kind, method) but then does ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log), putting the base logger instead of `log` into the context. All downstream log calls and the storage call lose the name/kind/method fields, hampering debugging. It should pass `log`.
